title: the-artifact-door-writes-a-json-record-in-one-canonical-form
intention: The artifact door writes a JSON record of truth in one canonical form, or refuses it: bytes for a .json path inside its jurisdiction that do not parse, or that are not the canonical serialisation (indent=2) of what they parse to, never land.
why: A record of truth must never silently land malformed (Law 7): on 2026-10-05 `cairn artifact write` accepted an indent=1 ticket (48c0c58a1714), and the shape check that exists only in transitions fired at the next phase write, after commit — test_transitions sealed red and a whole session's be4a crossing stalled until the ticket was reshaped by hand. The lived symptom is a voyage blocked by a record nobody can phase-write.
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth is never silently malformed) and Law 4 (a rule that matters is physics — transitions._ticket_shape already demands indent=2, but only at the NEXT write, after the bad bytes are committed); RULE 1 (the check lives in the artifact tool, the one door every record write rides)
how: In cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py write(): when the path is journaled (locate() hits) and ends in .json, parse the blob and compare it with json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=a) + optional newline for the shapes the corpus holds; refuse a mismatch with ValueError naming the path and the shape found, writing and journaling nothing. write_json already produces the canonical form, so its callers pass unchanged. A census of every journaled .json record in both repos runs first, so the accepted set is the measured corpus shape rather than a guess. Proof at cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/, written red.
falsifier: GREEN when a proof under cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/ shows: (1) write() of an indent=1 JSON body to a journaled .json path raises and leaves the file and journal unchanged; (2) an unparseable body to a journaled .json path raises; (3) the canonical indent=2 body lands and journals; (4) a non-.json record (a .md) and a path outside the jurisdiction are written as before; and the census of journaled .json records in both repos finds every one canonical. WRONG INTENT if some record class legitimately needs another shape (the census shows it), in which case the accepted set is per-class and declared, not one form.
watchme: none, because the consumer is cairn/tools/base/transitions.py _ticket_shape: once the door refuses non-canonical bytes, its IllegalTransition 'serialisation cannot be reproduced' stops firing, which the tester's test_transitions seal under cairn/tools/base/validations/ shows
children: none, because the build is one function's check in one file of one component with one proof
